cues.en: Let's talk about our next developer fundamentals.
cues.zh: 來談下一個開發者基本功。

cues.en: And this one is understanding data structures.
cues.zh: 就是理解資料結構。

cues.en: A really good programmer is a programmer that is able to decide what data structure to use when.
cues.zh: 優秀的程式設計師，能判斷什麼時候該用哪種資料結構。

cues.en: Up until now, we've learned about dictionaries and lists and we'll learn about a couple more throughout the course.
cues.zh: 目前學過字典和串列，整門課還會學幾種。

cues.en: But a really good programmer, a programmer who's experienced, is able to understand what the tradeoffs are, when to use what.
cues.zh: 但有經驗的好程式設計師，能理解各種取捨，知道何時使用什麼。

cues.en: And although I can give you a list of this is when you should do this and this is when you should use maybe dictionaries.
cues.zh: 雖然我可以列個清單，說這時用這個、那時可能該用字典，

cues.en: The thing is, this takes practice and experience.
cues.zh: 但其實這需要練習和經驗。

cues.en: So throughout our course and then the exercises that we're going to do, the projects we're going to build at the end, I hope that this idea of understanding when to use what data structure makes sense
cues.zh: 希望透過課程、接下來的練習，以及最後要打造的專案，選擇資料結構這個概念，能讓你

cues.en: to you.
cues.zh: 逐漸理解。

cues.en: But let's go back to our example.
cues.zh: 回到例子。

cues.en: When should you use a list and when should you use a dictionary?
cues.zh: 什麼時候用串列，什麼時候用字典？

cues.en: Well, the first thing we have to realize that a dictionary is not sorted, right?
cues.zh: 首先，講者這裡認為字典沒有排序，對吧？

cues.en: A list has order, it has zero one indexes, so on and so forth.
cues.zh: 串列有順序，有索引 0、1，依此類推。

cues.en: A dictionary has no order.
cues.zh: 講者把字典描述為沒有順序。

cues.en: So maybe if you want to have a list of people in line your shop, well, you should probably use a list,
cues.zh: 如果要記錄店裡排隊的人，可能該用串列。

cues.en: but maybe you have a user that is playing a game and that user has first name, maybe weapons, maybe an H that doesn't have to be ordered.
cues.zh: 但如果有位遊戲使用者，包含名字、武器、年齡，這些資訊不一定需要依序排列，

cues.en: So you might use a dictionary.
cues.zh: 就可能用字典。

cues.en: Also, you'll notice that dictionaries hold more information than lists.
cues.zh: 你也會發現，字典能表達比串列更多的資訊，

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: Because lists only have that single value.
cues.zh: 因為串列項目只有那個值，

cues.en: That is a list, has the index, and then whatever the value is.
cues.zh: 也就是索引，以及對應的值。

cues.en: And here we have a dictionary inside of a list which is holding a lot of information.
cues.zh: 這裡則是串列中有字典，容納很多資訊。

cues.en: Deep down, a list is simply an index and some sort of value here.
cues.zh: 基本上，串列就是索引和對應的值，

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧。

cues.en: Versus a dictionary that holds a lot more information.
cues.zh: 相較之下，字典還包含更多資訊。

cues.en: It holds a key.
cues.zh: 它有鍵，

cues.en: So this could be the weapons of that user.
cues.zh: 所以這可能是使用者的武器，

cues.en: Hello.
cues.zh: Hello

cues.en: Can be the greeting of that user.
cues.zh: 可以是使用者的問候語，

cues.en: Maybe is.
cues.zh: 也許 is_

cues.en: Magic is another information about that user.
cues.zh: magic 是使用者的另一項資訊。

cues.en: So we're able to have both keys and values in a dictionary.
cues.zh: 所以字典能同時表達鍵和值，

cues.en: So it holds a lot more information.
cues.zh: 因此有更多描述資訊。

cues.en: And as we learn different data structures, you'll have these different pros and cons, you'll start to understand as to when to use what.
cues.zh: 隨著學到不同資料結構，你會知道各自優缺點，開始了解什麼時候該用哪個。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.zh: 這就是另一個開發者基本功，下支影片見。

cues.zh: 再見。
